FADE IN:

INT. VETERAN'S BEDROOM - DAY

We see a small, cluttered bedroom. There's a bed, a dresser, and a few pieces of furniture scattered around. The walls are adorned with old photographs and war memorabilia. We see a WW1 veteran, JIM (60s), lying in bed, looking confused. He's dressed in a worn-out uniform, and his hair is thinning.

JIM
(to himself)
What's my name? What's my name?

He looks around the room, trying to remember something. Suddenly, he sees a photograph on the dresser.

JIM
(excitedly)
Oh, yes! I remember! I was at the front lines! I was with my unit...

He looks at the photograph, trying to recall the details. But his mind is a blank.

JIM
(frustrated)
No, no, no... I don't remember anything.

He looks around the room again, trying to find something to trigger his memory. He sees a small, leather-bound book on the nightstand.

JIM
(excitedly)
Ah, yes! My journal! I wrote about the war in this...

He opens the book, but it's filled with blank pages.

JIM
(disappointed)
No... no... I don't remember writing anything.

He looks up, and sees a man standing in the doorway. It's a young man, probably in his early 20s.

JIM
(confused)
Who are you?

MAN
Hi, Mr. Jim. My name is John. I'm a nurse.

JIM
(confused)
Nurse? What do you mean?

MAN
You're a veteran, Mr. Jim. You were in the war.

JIM
(confused)
War? What war?

MAN
World War I.

JIM
(confused)
No... no... I don't remember anything.

The man tries to help Jim remember, but it's no use. Jim's mind is a complete blank.

JIM
(frustrated)
I don't remember anything! I don't remember my name! I don't remember anything!

The man tries to comfort Jim, but it's clear that he's struggling to cope with his memories.

MAN
It's okay, Mr. Jim. You're safe now. You're in a hospital.

JIM
(confused)
Hospital? What hospital?

MAN
You're at a hospital in London. You were brought here after the war.

JIM
(confused)
War? What war?

The man tries to explain, but Jim's mind is a complete blank. He looks around the room, trying to find something to trigger his memory. Suddenly, he sees a photograph on the dresser.

JIM
(excitedly)
Oh, yes! I remember! I was at the front lines! I was with my unit...

But as he looks at the photograph, he sees a man getting shot in the head. His brains fall out from the back of his head.

JIM
(horrified)
No... no... no...

The man tries to comfort Jim, but it's clear that he's having a flashback.

MAN
Mr. Jim, it's okay. It's just a memory. It's not real.

JIM
(confused)
What's real? What's not real?

The man tries to explain, but Jim's mind is a complete blank. He looks around the room, trying to find something to trigger his memory. But it's no use. He's lost in a sea of confusion and forgetfulness.

FADE TO BLACK.
